entries.content:
The Space Pirates are the chief enemies of the Galactic Federation and the recurring adversaries of Samus Aran. They are described as a species of warring bipedal organisms, but the name covers an organization as much as a race: the crab-clawed Zebesians who conquered Zebes, the insectoid Kihunters who came from another galactic system to help rebuild it, and the troopers of Tallon IV, Aether and the Pirate Homeworld are all Space Pirates. They employ other creatures as leaders: they took Zebes with Mother Brain, and count Ridley, Kraid and the general Weavel among their leaders. Weavel, critically wounded in a clash with Samus, was rebuilt as a cyborg and fought on as a bounty hunter. Their planet of origin is unknown; even the Pirate Homeworld is not confirmed as their birthplace.

Their trade is piracy and conquest. Per the manual (Super Metroid) they are "the scourge of the Galaxy," known for stealing galactic trading ships and leaving the crews stranded in space. Per the manga, Pirates led by Ridley raided the colony K-2L and killed Samus's parents. Their defining crime was the theft of the Metroid specimen from a Federation research vessel returning from SR388; they carried it to their fortress on Zebes, where, per the original manual, the Federation feared they would multiply the creatures with beta rays. The Federation's assault on Zebes failed, and Samus was sent in alone.

Their history in brief:
- Zebes: Samus defeated Kraid, Ridley and Mother Brain and escaped the Space Pirate Mother Ship (Metroid: Zero Mission). Three research frigates, Orpheon among them, fled with Metroid cargo.
- Tallon IV: the survivors mined Phazon, ran Project Helix and rebuilt Ridley as Meta Ridley until Samus wiped out the operation.
- Aether: Pirates who found Phazon in the Dasha System built a base there and raided Dark Aether for ore; overpowered by the Ing and the hunters, they abandoned the mining facility, which the Federation later dismantled.
- The Phazon crisis: the crew of the battleship Colossus acquired the remains of Dark Samus, who revived herself on their Phazon, killed a third of them and made the rest her disciples. The Pirates seized Aurora Unit 313, attacked Norion, Bryyo and Elysia, and were crushed when the Federation stormed the Pirate Homeworld and Phaaze was destroyed.
- Afterward: Pirates regrouping in the Bermuda System built the battleship Doomseye; the Federation Force disabled its shield and the Federation fleet destroyed it.
- Ridley and his Pirates stole the baby Metroid from the Ceres Space Colony and fled to a rebuilt Zebes; Samus followed, killed Ridley and Mother Brain, and the planet exploded.
- Later: Cyborg Zebesians cloned by the Federation aboard the Bottle Ship; the rogue hunter Sylux and his army of Space Pirates, who attacked Federation research facilities including one on the planet Tanamaar in the Desolan System; and X Parasite mimics on the BSL station.

Pirate culture, known mostly from their own Pirate Data logs, is disciplined, obedient and bureaucratic; troopers are "ruthless and amoral," trained to follow orders without question. The Pirates call Samus "the Hunter" and have offered a bounty for her, dead or alive, since the fall of Zebes.
entries.notes: Corrected per fact-check: Doomseye destroyed by the Federation fleet after the Federation Force disabled its shield; Tanamaar is a planet in the Desolan System; 'flagship' replaced with 'Pirates led by Ridley'; Aether outcome now follows Metroid Wiki ('overpowered by the Ing and the Hunters', facility abandoned and later dismantled). The Super Metroid manual's trading-ships clause was confirmed on Metroid Wiki's Zebesian page. The Beyond claim that the Pirates are controlled by Metroids is an 'it is believed' passage on Metroid Wiki and was dropped. Weavel added (Metroid Wiki leaders list; official Hunters site). Kraid is listed by Metroid Wiki among Pirate leaders; Mother Brain under 'Took over Zebes with Mother Brain'. Consistency pass: Sylux's Tanamaar attack moved after the return to Zebes and the Bottle Ship, matching the timeline entry (Beyond falls between Other M and Fusion); 'Ceres Station' normalized to 'Ceres Space Colony'.

entries.comment: Space Pirates: Organization, High Command and Science Team
entries.content:
The Space Pirate Organization runs as a rigid military bureaucracy. At the top sits Command, the highest tier of the hierarchy; Pirate records name High Command and subdivisions including Facility Command, Security Command, Central Command, Mine Security Command, Operations Command and Energy Command. High Command authorizes Phazon programs, approves reinforcements and sets timetables, and its patience is short: "Command grows impatient regarding this matter: results must be produced soon." The logs never name its individual members. On Zebes the Pirates answered to Mother Brain; Ridley has led their forces in the field and, rebuilt as Meta Ridley, served as a mainstay of Pirate security; by the Phazon crisis the whole organization had been subsumed by Dark Samus, whose followers called themselves her disciples.

Beneath Command is the Science Team, the research and development branch, with sub-units such as Research Team Sclera, which combined a Phazon strain called Vertigo with Pirate DNA and made Project Helix work. Science Team studied Phazon, Metroids, Chozo relics and Samus's own weapons, usually under hard deadlines and with heavy losses of staff and test subjects.

The military is a caste system, recorded most clearly during the Phazon crisis (Metroid Prime 3: Corruption), rising from the expendable Pirate Militia through Pirate Troopers and the elite Commando Pirates to the ruling caste of Pirate Commanders (see Pirate military of the Phazon crisis). Under Dark Samus, Gandrayda herself moved among the troops in their form, watching for signs of weakness, and several unfaithful disciples were "ended...violently."

The Pirate Data shows a culture both obedient and darkly comic: troopers trained "to follow orders without question," which made them ideal hosts for the Ing on Aether; workers struck by Phazon madness, from muscle spasms to hallucinations; Gronkats and Olbaps ordered disposed of after domestic beasts proved susceptible to the madness; Metroid handlers on Aether reminded that "Metroids are not pets. Metroids are not target practice," and that unauthorized feeding remained strictly prohibited; and an entire shift of Phazon-maddened Dynamo workers handed to the Elite Pirates as training adversaries. Samus has recovered these records with her Scan Visor; they are the main window outsiders have into how Pirates think.
entries.notes: Unverifiable quote 'Failure to comply with Command decree is not an option' replaced with the confirmed Chozo Artifacts log line. Command subdivision names follow Metroid Wiki's Command page. Gandrayda (not 'officers') moved among the troops, per the 'Mistress Gandrayda' log. Militia promotion removed (cut-content source). Training adversaries corrected to Dynamo workers; Phazon madness symptoms per the Mining Status log (no violence). The Gronkat/Olbap disposal order is a Metroid Prime scan in the Central Dynamo, not an Echoes scan. Metroid Handling Protocols quote from the Biostorage Station page per the fact-check. Consistency pass: caste list trimmed to a one-sentence pointer; the Militia rumor, Commander tenure and caste details live in 'Pirate military of the Phazon crisis'.

Kihunter manual quote corrected to the Super Metroid manual's actual wording ('pirates from another galactic system who helped rebuild Zebes'; 'When they lose their wings, they spit powerful acid'). Larva/pupa corrected per Metroid Wiki: Zero is the larva, Zoro the pupal form (the draft called the Zoro the larva). Zero Mission appearance kept: Metroid Wiki's Zebesian page lists Zero Mission. Black Zebesian Charge Beam weakness restored. Gold Zebesian mimics in the BSL incident added per the fact-check (Pirate Trooper page). Redundant keys (Cyborg Zebesian, King Kihunter, Super Zebesian) dropped because the base keys already match them; Zoro/Zoros added. The Space Pirate 'scourge' manual quote now lives in the overview only; the Fusion manual quote was cut for length.

entries.comment: Space Pirates: Troop types of Tallon IV and Aether
entries.content:
The Space Pirates Samus fought on Tallon IV and Aether were organized into specialized troop types, most recorded in her Scan Visor logbook.

- Pirate Troopers are the common infantry, a "sentient aggressor species well trained in weapon and melee combat," ruthless and amoral. On Tallon IV they carried Galvanic Accelerator Cannons and forearm Scythes; on Aether a Photonic Power Scythe and Quantum Assault Cannon became standard issue.
- Beam Troopers (Power, Wave, Ice and Plasma Troopers) wore armor and arms copied from Samus's beams, reverse-engineered from combat data because "Command would dearly enjoy turning Aran's weapons against her." Each could be harmed only by the beam it carried. They served in the Phazon Mines and answered the Omega Pirate's summons.
- Flying Pirates, jet-pack troops of the Tallon Overworld, Magmoor Caverns and Phendrana Drifts, fired beams and missiles; their packs showed on thermal imaging, and one whose pack failed hurled itself at its attacker. Aqua Pirates, their underwater counterpart in the flooded wreck of the Orpheon, rammed their target the same way when their armor failed.
- Shadow Pirates of Phendrana and the Mines carried cloaking generators so power-hungry that they fought only with scythes; thermal or X-ray imaging or a Wave Beam shot exposed them.
- Pirate Aerotroopers succeeded the Flying Pirates on Aether, "known for their cold precision and utter cruelty," armed with homing missiles and preferring a suicide strike to capture.
- Pirate Commandos, the elite of Aether, were "dedicated to 'hunting the Hunter'," with energy scythes, pulse cannons, EMP grenade launchers, thrusters and a short-lived barrier shield; Samus first met them at Torvus Grove.
- Pirate Grenadiers carried an experimental energy grenade launcher too bulky to pair with rifles or scythes and rammed anyone who closed in. Samus met only two pairs, in the Agon Wastes Command Center and on the Temple Grounds' Path of Eyes.

On Aether the Ing found Pirate Troopers, "already trained to follow orders without question," perfect hosts. Dark Pirate Troopers fought Samus in the Agon Wastes, Dark Agon and the Temple Grounds. Dark Pirate Commandos, possessed only by Hunter Ing, who competed for the right and lent them the power to phase out of local timespace, haunted Torvus Bog, Dark Torvus Bog, the Temple Grounds and the Ing Hive. In the Sanctuary Fortress Samus watched Dark Samus slaughter a group of Dark Pirate Troopers. (Metroid Prime; Metroid Prime 2: Echoes)
entries.notes: Dark Pirate Commando locations corrected (Torvus Bog, Dark Torvus Bog, Temple Grounds, Ing Hive; none in Agon). Unit locations for Flying Pirates, Shadow Pirates and Grenadiers added per the fact-check. 'Dark Pirate Trooper' and 'Dark Pirate Commando' are matched by the 'Pirate Trooper'/'Pirate Commando' keys, so they are not listed separately. Metroid Wiki titles the Beam Trooper page 'Trooper Pirate'. Aerotroopers are keyed in the Phazon-crisis military entry. The Metroid-bait claim (citation needed on the wiki) stays omitted.

entries.comment: Space Pirates: Pirate military of the Phazon crisis (Militia, Commandos, Commanders)
entries.content:
After Dark Samus seized the Space Pirate Organization and seeded the Pirate Homeworld with Phazon, the Pirate military was rebuilt around Phazon (Metroid Prime 3: Corruption). Most regular troops carried Phazon Enhancement Devices and could enter Hypermode, becoming faster and tougher, though Phazon-based weapons still harmed them. Standard kit was an Assault Rifle and Energy Scythe, "both powered by Phazon," plus EMP Grenades, a Dash Jet and a short-lived hover system. Armor was graded: Armored Pirate Troopers resisted beams but not Missiles; Advanced Pirate Troopers wore thick Phazite; Assault Pirate Troopers wore missile-resistant armor and favored melee; Shield Pirate Troopers carried energy shields that Samus's Grapple Lasso could tear away. Most served on the Homeworld, with detachments on Bryyo, Elysia and Norion.

Phazite, a Phazon-derived armor, marks the upper castes. Commando Pirates, found only on the Homeworld, wore Phazite that "only Beams of the highest temperature can penetrate," with a cloaking field, boost thrusters and a personal teleporter. Samus's X-Ray Visor and Nova Beam let her strike the head through the helmet, though Hypermode interfered with the lock-on; a Commando stripped of its Phazite lost its cloak and fought like an ordinary trooper. Pirate Commanders, the ruling caste, each a Commando for at least ten years, wore more resilient red Phazite, teleported around the field and called Commandos to their side; Phazon attacks hurt both castes. One Commander ambushed Samus and Admiral Dane's Demolition Troopers on the Homeworld, badly wounded her, and died at her hands.

Aerotroopers, successors to the Flying Pirates, had served on Aether; in the Phazon crisis they traded armor for evasion, fighting with twin Remote Attack Pods that fired Particle Cannons and Helix Missiles, plus sticky Gel Bombs. Their code amounts to death before dishonor, ending in a spinning suicide attack that Ice Missiles can stop. Plasma Beam fire ignites an Aerotrooper's jetpack so the Grapple Lasso can tear it from the pilot.

At the bottom stood the Pirate Militia, expendable infantry recruited from the Homeworld's slaves and criminals, denied Phazon Enhancement Devices, armed with weaker arm cannons and retractable scythes, and "surprisingly obedient to the upper castes"; rumor held that disobedient Militia became dinner for regular troopers. Samus first met them aboard the G.F.S. Olympus during the Pirate raid, then on Norion, Bryyo and Elysia. Pirate ground forces rode into battle aboard Space Pirate Armored Tactical Carriers and Boarding Pods.
entries.notes: 'Lighter packs' replaced with Metroid Wiki's 'traded armor for evasion'. Militia first met aboard the Olympus, then Norion (Militia are not recorded as encountered on the Homeworld). Full name 'Space Pirate Armored Tactical Carrier' used. Added the Aerotrooper Plasma Beam/Grapple Lasso and Ice Missile counters and the Commando cloak-loss and Hypermode lock-on details per the fact-check. Gandrayda-as-Aerotrooper sentence cut (not re-verified). The Aerotrooper Hypermode-warp contradiction and unused Advanced/Assault Militia remain omitted.

entries.comment: Space Pirates: Elite Pirates and the Omega Pirate
entries.content:
Elite Pirates were the product of Project Helix, the Space Pirate program to splice Phazon into Pirate DNA. Science Team expected "radical new Pirate genomes" while admitting that "Phazon madness is a concern." The first embryo infusions at Glacier One were disastrous: Phazon degenerated brain tissue even as it built muscle, most subjects died before maturing, and the survivors turned violent. The breakthrough came when Research Team Sclera combined a Phazon strain called Vertigo with Pirate DNA. In the Phazon Mines the Elites, larger, stronger and far more resilient than ordinary Pirates, were fed Elite Ration Mix and trained against an entire shift of Phazon-maddened Dynamo workers. In simulations they scored a 74% success ratio against Samus Aran; High Command was pleased but expected a higher ratio by the project's end, and predicted that Elites, alongside ordinary and Flying Pirates, would form a "near-indestructible backbone."

An Elite carries a shoulder-mounted Plasma Artillery Cannon, a Repulsion Shield, a Wave Quake Generator that sends shock waves across the ground, retractable Wrist Bayonets and an energy-siphon system that drinks beam fire to feed the cannon. Its weaknesses are slowness, a cannon whose heat shows on thermal imaging, and vulnerability to concussive weapons such as Missiles. Seven Elite Pirates were stationed throughout the Mines, and Samus fought three. In Elite Research a Power Bomb freed the Phazon Elite, ident-code EPG-8642, "Elite Pirate Alpha," a cannonless Elite infused with energized Phazon whose shortened lifespan the researchers deemed "of little concern"; killing it won Samus the Artifact of Warrior.

The pinnacle was Elite Pirate Upsilon, code-named the Omega Pirate, kept in cryosleep in the Elite Quarters above a pool of Phazon. Dosed far beyond safety limits, its mass "increased exponentially" while it "retained all mental faculties." It healed by coating itself in Phazon, a Chameleon Manta cloaking device hid it while it fed, and it could summon Beam Troopers. Its absorption system handled beams but not Missiles, a "critical design flaw," and no simulated subject lived beyond two deca-cycles, so lifespans had to improve before the design could be cost-effective. Samus woke it, shattered the Phazon plates on its knees and shoulders, tracked it through its cloak with the X-Ray Visor, and killed it. The dying Omega Pirate collapsed onto her, and its Phazon fused with her armor to create the Phazon Suit, which later let her channel the Phazon Beam (Metroid Prime).
entries.notes: 74% ratio corrected: High Command was pleased but expected more. Omega Pirate lifespan line corrected (lifespans had to improve for cost-effectiveness; no claim the team doubted it). Training adversaries are Dynamo workers. 'Mass production' replaced with the Special Forces log's backbone prediction. 'Seven in stasis' changed to 'seven stationed throughout the Mines'. Phazon Beam added per the fact-check. Redundant keys (Elite Pirate Upsilon/Alpha) replaced with plurals. The Omega Pirate is also covered from the encounter side in the prime1 domain.

entries.comment: Space Pirates: Projects and Phazon research on Tallon IV and Aether
entries.content:
The Space Pirates came to Tallon IV after detecting energy readings on "a Wanderer-class planet identified as Tallon IV." The source proved to be Phazon, an unstable and immensely potent radioactive mutagen, and Science Team judged the world "a viable secondary headquarters" after the fall of Zebes. The Phazon Program was their bid to "rise dominant of this sector within a deca-cycle." Yields climbed 44%, but Phazon madness, with loss of equilibrium, muscle spasms and, in extreme cases, hallucinations, forced stricter safety rules.

Facilities:
- Glacier One in Phendrana Drifts, the research headquarters, with Research Lab Hydra, Research Lab Aether and an Observatory; the cold kept captive Metroids sluggish.
- The Phazon Mines, the headquarters proper, reached through the crashed Orpheon, with Elite Research, Metroid Quarantine and the Central Dynamo.

Projects recorded in the Pirate Data (Metroid Prime):
- Metroid Studies: Phazon infusion of the Metroids saved from Zebes showed "a considerable growth in power and size"; Science Team proposed taming them, since "a small force of disciplined Metroids could wipe out entire armies."
- Parasite infusion: Phazon made Tallon IV's Parasites larger and more aggressive but wiped them out by the fourth infusion period; mutated Parasite Queens aboard the Orpheon were the best result.
- Project Titan: exposing inanimate matter to Phazon produced the rock creature Thardus; after security breaches with massive casualties the project was suspended indefinitely.
- Project Helix: Phazon spliced into Pirate DNA, yielding the Elite Pirates and the Omega Pirate.
- Hunter Weapons: Samus's arsenal reverse-engineered from combat data; beam copies armed the Beam Troopers, but four test subjects "were horribly broken" by Morph Ball prototypes.
- Chozo Studies: the Pirates set out to strip the Chozo Ruins and breach the Impact Crater's containment field, though Chozo Ghosts assaulted their personnel and "few have survived." Their creed: "The dead should serve the living, not hinder them."

On Aether, Pirates who found Phazon in the Dasha System located a Rift Portal and the Dark Beam and began raiding Dark Aether for ore, while experimenting on captive Tallon Metroids, trying to domesticate them and draining them for bio-energy (Metroid Prime 2: Echoes). The sickness there was logged as Phazon Fever: Technician 12 claimed the Phazon as his own and held off the staff with a weapon until security arrived. Samus destroyed these programs in person, and the Phazon the Pirates coveted later nearly consumed her.
entries.notes: Fission/Hunter Metroid attribution removed (Metroid Wiki does not credit either strain to Pirate work); replaced with the confirmed Metroid Studies line. 'Violence' removed from Phazon madness symptoms. Technician 12 incident restated per the Medical Report 07.199.09 summary on the Phazon Fever page. Aether Metroids: experimentation, domestication and bio-energy draining, not breeding. 'Only' route through the Orpheon softened. 'Wanderer-class' and 'viable secondary headquarters' come from the Contact log; Chozo Ghost assaults from the Elite Control log. Trimmed from 530 words to the 400-word budget; the Metroid Prime creature is left to the prime1 domain.

entries.comment: Space Pirates: Ships and the Frigate Orpheon
entries.content:
At the fall of Zebes three research frigates, Orpheon, Siriacus and Vol Paragom, "were in orbit at zero hour and managed to retreat" with the Pirates' surviving Metroids. Orpheon's Metroids all survived; the ship docked at Vortex Outpost, then took orbit over Tallon IV to collect native life for Phazon experiments. Its mutated Parasite Queens were its greatest success and its doom: two broke containment and killed most of the crew, and the survivors lit a distress beacon and abandoned ship. Samus answered the beacon and killed the remaining Queen, whose body fell into the reactor and set off the self-destruct; escaping, she saw Meta Ridley flee toward the planet. The wreck crashed on Tallon IV, where its flooded hull, prowled by Aqua Pirates, became a road into the Phazon Mines (Metroid Prime).

Other Pirate craft:
- The Space Pirate Mother Ship in Chozodia on Zebes, whose forces shot down Samus's gunship; she infiltrated it in her Zero Suit armed only with a Paralyzer, destroyed Mecha Ridley, and escaped in a Pirate ship as it self-destructed.
- A Pirate frigate crippled by a Federation patrol, which crashed on Aether.
- The battleship Colossus, "used for battle and storage purposes." Its crew failed to intercept the G.F.S. Anhur, salvaged the Phazon the Federation left behind, and revived Dark Samus. Improved under her, its "Phazon-powered weapons" rendered the G.F.S. Valhalla helpless; the Pirates seized Aurora Unit 313 and, by their own account, jettisoned the crew into space. Its later fate is unknown.
- The Leviathan battleship: finding the Colossus not intimidating enough, Dark Samus had a Leviathan fitted with cybernetic weapons, its crew quarters and command consoles placed within the beast's skull. The Federation later seized it to reach Phaaze.
- Boarding Pods, nicknamed Space Coffins: crude craft with an explosive nose cone that rams enemy hulls, as dangerous to their crews as to the target, used in the raid on the G.F.S. Olympus.
- Space Pirate Armored Tactical Carriers (ATCs), troop craft with Tribeam cannons and a single vulnerable heat vent, deployed over Norion and SkyTown.
- The Doomseye, a colossal battleship built by Pirates regrouping in the Bermuda System, aboard which they held a brainwashed, enlarged Samus until the Federation Force freed her and the Federation fleet destroyed the ship (see The Doomseye).
entries.notes: Self-destruct corrected: the Parasite Queen's body fell into the reactor. Wiki inferences removed (Aqua Pirates 'searching for survivors'; Colossus 'scrapped', which Metroid Wiki marks as purported). Valhalla's 'Phazon-powered weapons' confirmed in the 'Taking Valhalla' log. Added the crashed Aether frigate (Captain A. Exeter's report) and the Colossus's earlier plans. Keys added for Colossus, Vol Paragom, Space Coffin and Pirate ATC; bare 'ATC' avoided as too generic, and 'Frigate Orpheon'/'Space Pirate Mother Ship' are matched by 'Orpheon'/'Pirate Mother Ship'. Closing Phaaze fleet-battle sentence and 'Ridley's vessel' cut for length and caution. Parasite Queen detail is left mainly to the prime1 domain. Consistency pass: the crew's jettisoning is now attributed to the Pirates' own 'Taking Valhalla' log, since Samus found Marines' bodies aboard the wreck (federation and prime3 entries; Metroid Wiki G.F.S. Valhalla page). Doomseye bullet trimmed to a pointer and its key left to the federation-force Doomseye entry.

entries.content:
The Pirate Homeworld is the fortified planet from which the Space Pirates waged the Phazon crisis (Metroid Prime 3: Corruption). The name is a designation, not a confirmed origin: nothing establishes it as the species' birthplace. Its low-pH atmosphere produces acid rain that penetrates Samus's armor; she obtained the Hazard Shield on the planet itself before she could cross its open courtyards.

After Dark Samus took the Pirates, the Homeworld was the first world she seeded: a Leviathan struck it, and the Pirates rejoiced at being "the first world to receive this blessing," expecting "thousands of new disciples." It became the base for their assaults on Norion, Bryyo and Elysia, guarded by a planetary shield, Commando Pirates and Pirate Commanders of the ruling caste, and laced with transit systems linking sectors such as Pirate Mines and Pirate Command, where the Command Courtyard lies. Its slaves and criminals filled the ranks of the Pirate Militia.

Samus came to the Homeworld after destroying the Leviathans of Bryyo and Elysia. Gandrayda, sent to locate the planet, had been corrupted by Phazon there; she now moved among the Pirates in their own form, watching for weakness, and had vowed to present Samus's "bloody helmet" to Dark Samus. Posing as a Federation Marine, she lured Samus into a trap and fought her on a tower in the acid rain; defeated, she shifted uncontrollably through the forms of a Space Pirate, Ghor, Rundas and Samus before Dark Samus absorbed her. Samus then disabled the planetary shield with the Nova Beam and X-Ray Visor, letting Admiral Dane's fleet land. Demolition Troopers blasted a path through a transit line with no train toward the Leviathan Seed, and a Pirate Commander who ambushed them badly wounded Samus before she killed him. Inside the Seed, Omega Ridley guarded the core; Samus destroyed both, and the Federation took the Pirates' Leviathan battleship and used it to open a wormhole to Phaaze.

The Pirate Data, from "Our Mission" to "Mistress Gandrayda," records the Pirates' fall from Phazon hunters to Dark Samus's cult, including the boast "If Samus comes to our Homeworld, she will find us ready."
entries.notes: Urtraghus and SN-883 removed (no fetchable source confirms their status). Militia no longer listed among the Homeworld's defenders; only their recruitment there is stated. 'Pirate Research' sector and the Command Courtyard as 'hub' removed; Pirate Mines and Pirate Command are confirmed area names (Pirate Trooper page). Added Gandrayda's corruption on the planet and her death (Gandrayda page per the fact-check), the Hazard Shield's acquisition on the Homeworld, and the Nova Beam/X-Ray Visor shield shutdown. The Aurora Unit 313 seed-launch claim and the 'Vanguard' label were cut as unverified. 'Acid rain' dropped as a key (too generic). The wormhole is credited to the stolen Leviathan battleship per Wikipedia and Metroid Wiki.

entries.comment: Space Pirates: The Pirates and Samus (the Hunter)
entries.content:
To the Space Pirates, Samus Aran is "the Hunter." Per the manga, the enmity began at K-2L, where Pirates led by Ridley raided the colony: Virginia Aran died shielding her daughter, Rodney Aran died igniting the Afloraltite aboard the Pirate ship, and Samus was the only survivor. Per the manga, years later on Jigrad, serving with the Federation Police, she nearly executed a surrendering Pirate in her rage ("Did you say...'Mercy'!?") before arresting him "in the name of the Federation Police."

The Pirates' own records treat her as a problem to be solved. After the fall of Zebes, survivors reported ground personnel killed "by the Hunter clad in metal," and a Security Command all-points alert described a heavily armed female hominid in a powered armorsuit: "A considerable bounty will go to the unit who delivers Aran to Command. Dead or alive, it matters not." Science Team copied her arsenal for the Beam Troopers and tested Elite Pirates against simulations of her; High Command was pleased with a 74% success ratio but wanted better. On Aether a confused garrison watched a hunter in dark armor steal their Phazon, nicknamed her the "Dark Hunter," and, when a second armored hunter arrived and the two fought, proposed allying with one against the other; the logs never identify the Dark Hunter as Dark Samus.

During the Phazon crisis the crew of the Colossus swore to "take that Phazon or die trying." Their logs record defeats: "The Hunter's might is great, and she is as efficient as ever when it comes to disrupting our operations" (Bryyo), and "The accursed Elysian machines were no match for Aran's guns." They noted that the hunters struck down on Norion each bore Dark Samus's "mark of corruption," and Gandrayda vowed to lay Samus's bloody helmet before Dark Samus.

Samus's side of the ledger: she defeated Kraid, Ridley and Mother Brain on Zebes; critically wounded the Pirate general Weavel, who returned as a cyborg; dismantled Pirate operations on Tallon IV, Aether and the Pirate Homeworld, where a Pirate Commander badly wounded her before she killed him; was captured, brainwashed and enlarged by the Pirates of the Doomseye until the Federation Force freed her; pursued Ridley to a rebuilt Zebes to recover the stolen baby Metroid, a mission that ended with the planet's destruction; and fought Sylux's Pirates at the Federation facility on Tanamaar.
entries.notes: Selective entry: generic primary keys fire only alongside a Pirate-related secondary key (restricted words appear only as secondary disambiguators). Fixes: 74% ratio pleased High Command; 'Hunter clad in metal' attributed to the Fall of Zebes log and the bounty quote to the Security Command alert; 'flagship' removed; Commander superlative replaced with 'badly wounded her'; the unverifiable Super Metroid manual quote 'to finish them off' dropped; 'never grasped' softened to what the logs say. Added the Federation Police arrest on Jigrad and Weavel. The draft's editorial line about Samus's restraint was removed as unsupported. 'Dark Hunter' needs a secondary hit to fire; accepted trade-off since the Dark Samus domain covers that subject. Consistency pass: Tanamaar placed after the return to Zebes, matching the timeline entry.
